olivia (support): FYI customer eve reports p99 latency jump from ~450ms -> 2.1s on inference route /v1/generate around 13:20 UTC. Ticket #5473. They say it started after yesterday's model rollout. :frowning_face:
kevin (eng-runtime): Noted. Any host IDs or region? Is this hosted or dedicated?
olivia (support): Hosted, region=us-west-2. Customer attached a short trace and request ids: req_9f3a2, req_9f3b8. Said reruns are flaky — sometimes fast, sometimes 2s+.
samir (eng-sre): Pinging perf dashboards. @perf-bot can you pull p95/p99 for route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-large, region=us-west-2 for last 6h?
perf-bot: p95=520ms, p99=1.98s (6h window). Spike visible between 13:10-13:30 UTC. Eviction rate for kv-prefix-cache also spiked ~3x.
ad a (oncall): Reproduced quickly from our synthetic: observed cold prefix-cache miss ratio jumped from 8% -> 42% for sequences with long prefixes. Logs show prefix-key normalization churn (different casing + trailing spaces) for some traffic.
kevin (eng-runtime): That smells like cache key entropy. If prefix keys are not normalized consistently across routing, we will blow the prefix cache. Can we get a sample of keys for those request ids?
olivia (support): Customer attached the payloads, sending snippets in thread (redacted). They include user-supplied system prompts that occasionally have trailing whitespace.
kevin (eng-runtime): Found a small bug in prefix normalization introduced in yesterday's PR #4128 — we dropped a trim() in one fast path. That would create different keys for identical logical prefixes.
samir (eng-sre): That explains the eviction spike. High miss -> KV cache warmups -> more GPU work -> higher tail latency.
ada (oncall): For quick mitigation can we 1) rollback normalization change, or 2) increase prefix-cache size temporarily? What is cheaper?
kevin (eng-runtime): Rollback is safest short-term. But we can also push a runtime config to double prefix-cache entries for us-west-2 to absorb hotset while we ship a fix. Doubling will increase memory but buys time.
kevin (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate steps:
- revert PR #4128 (hotfix) -> deploy to canary + us-west-2
- temporary runtime config: prefix_cache.max_entries *= 2 for that region
- add normalization unit tests + fuzzing
- backfill warmup job to pre-populate hot prefixes for affected customers
ada (oncall): I'll start rollback. Running `deploy-rollback --service=runtime --rev=HEAD~1 --region=us-west-2` now.
perf-bot: Canary rollback deployed at 13:36 UTC. Canary p99 dropped to 620ms within 3 mins.
eve (customer): Thanks, we see much better numbers now. Will monitor and report if anything pops up. :raised_hands:
kevin (eng-runtime): Great. Follow-ups: add input trimming to normalization code path, add end-to-end test with synthetic trailing spaces, and add metric for "prefix_key_variants_per_logical_prefix" so we can detect entropy increases early.
samir (eng-sre): Also opening an incident doc for tracking RCA and postmortem. I'll attach latency graphs and eviction traces.
olivia (support): Closing the support escalation for now. Customer asked for a note when fix is live.
kevin (eng-runtime): I'll ship a proper fix + tests today and then a config that reverts the temporary doubling. Keeping metric alert threshold at >10 variants/logical-prefix for now.
ada (oncall): Marking this as resolved in PagerDuty runbook and adding a snippet to the runbook: how to query prefix-cache evictions and quick mitigation commands.
kevin (eng-runtime): Quick command to inspect evictions per shard:
```
kubectl exec -it runtime-cache-0 -- redis-cli info keyspace | grep prefix
# or
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?expr=kv_prefix_evictions{region=\"us-west-2\"}" | jq .
```
nolivia (support): Thanks all. I'll update ticket #5473 and ping customer when the fix lands. :thumbsup:
kevin (eng-runtime): Note: separate follow-up to consider switching eviction policy to LFU for prefix cache; LRU hurts when bursty hotsets oscillate. Will prototype next sprint.
perf-bot: Reminder: scheduled warmup job for top-100 prefixes runs at 03:00 UTC daily; we should consider increasing frequency for affected customers.
ad a (oncall): All done here. Reopen if p99 returns >1.5s.
